Agency hiring lens · Beta · 5 October 2026

Show the judgement.
Make the next step easy.

The portfolio communicates seniority, AI expertise and visual craft. Its next gains are earlier design evidence, a clearer agency offer and a shorter route from interest to an email.

Astra critique + live Chrome inspection. Desktop 1440 × 727. Mobile 390 × 844. Quick wins applied locally.

A credible senior partner.

An agency buyer can understand who you are and reach Contact from the sticky header. The bigger friction is building confidence efficiently: Home delays the work, some cases repeat their argument, and the small packages can undersell the role promised by the hero.

Identity: strongDistinctive serif, washed blue and restrained coral.

Contact: improvedDirect email is now prominent and copyable.

Time to value

Fit → proof → confidence → contact.

This is the agency buyer’s likely task path. These are expert judgements and observed page positions, not a usability study or a measured conversion uplift.

01 / Understand fit

“Can he help my team?”

Home answers this clearly: senior AI product design, agency teams, Madrid / Europe. Preserve that specificity.

02 / Inspect the work

“Is the design good?”

Home’s work grid begins at 1,415px desktop and 1,578px mobile. Its work CTA now goes straight to that selection. Work’s own images arrive earlier after this pass.

03 / Trust the contribution

“What did he decide?”

The shared contribution strip and design-judgement notes help. Next, align opening screenshots with the central decision in each story.

04 / Start a conversation

“How do I brief him?”

The persistent Contact link is already easy to find. The improved page now exposes direct email before logistical detail and explains the optional email helper.

Space has a job. Keep generous margins around the best evidence. Reduce the quiet lead-in before it. A 520px phone can demonstrate craft quickly, but on mobile it needs enough surrounding context to tell the viewer which project they are seeing.

Five decisions for Felipe

The choices worth making together.

The changes below affect positioning, page composition or the meaning of a case. They remain proposals. Select a direction and save your notes at the end.

01

Bring proof into Home’s opening.

The first desktop screen shows your proposition and portrait, but no client or product evidence. On mobile, the primary action appears at 620px and the work grid starts at 1,578px. A busy agency buyer must travel further than necessary to verify design quality.

RecommendationKeep the portrait and blur. Introduce a compact proof cue in the opening: selected brand names plus a visible route to one flagship AI case and one recognised brand. Let the work share more of the opening composition when we revisit it.

Trade-off: stronger early proof uses some of the current editorial breathing room. This decision concerns layout; the new portrait is still parked.

See the opening that delays product proof
Your direction
02

Let the offer match the senior role.

The site promises a senior AI product partner for a client brief, then presents up to four hours on a contained problem and sixteen hours per month. Those may be useful entry offers, but can make your available contribution feel smaller than the work demonstrates.

RecommendationLead with an agency project / embedded support conversation. Keep the smaller packages as secondary starting points if they still represent how you want to sell your time.

This needs your commercial judgement. Scope, availability and package terms should come from your real working model. The pass has not changed the hours or invented a new promise.

See how the current package frames your capacity
Your direction
03

Choose the primary contact mechanism.

The six-field helper has four required fields. It builds an email draft, then the visitor sends it from their own app. The explanation is now visible before the fields and direct email has a copy fallback, but the extra preparation remains.

RecommendationFor this static portfolio, make direct email the primary route and keep the brief helper optional. If you prefer a submitted enquiry, implement an actual form delivery service and a truthful confirmation state.

Trade-off: email is simple but depends on the visitor’s mail workflow; a genuine form reduces that dependency and brings a delivery, spam and data-handling responsibility.

Your direction
04

Use one mobile case-opening rhythm.

New Chat introduces its proposition before the phone. Services Hub, ENEM and Mi Mundo lead with a large portrait phone, pushing the title towards or below the first screen’s bottom. The shorter landscape Web app composition has less of this problem.

RecommendationUse a short project title and truthful status first, one large phone second, and the compact contribution strip next. Keep screens early and readable. Let the landscape case use the format its evidence needs.

Trade-off: image-first has immediate impact; context-first helps a visitor arriving from a direct link identify the work. The title block should stay compact.

See the mobile context delay
Your direction
05

Make the flagship story more selective.

New Chat is roughly 9,485px tall on desktop and 12,231px on mobile. Its entry, composer and history decisions recur across sections. The date-of-birth film is compelling, but leads the detailed story despite being a separate exploration outside the initial release.

RecommendationLead the detailed evidence with the chat flow, then show the voice exploration with its status intact. Keep one concise judgement beside each meaningful evidence group. Replace repetition with a distinct screen or remove the repeated passage.

The same editorial principle applies elsewhere: SkateKing should show discovery earlier; Card Dynamics should emphasise the partner/consent flow; Pizza Hut should show original service-design evidence where available. Related work stays before the final CTA as requested.

Applied quick wins

Less friction, already in the beta.

These are local changes to the current beta. Production has not been published or replaced by this pass.

Work starts with the work.

Shorter, clearer heading and smaller lead-in. The first two project covers now enter the desktop first screen.

Home’s secondary action is direct.

“See selected work” jumps to the selection already on Home. Sticky-header offsets keep anchor targets visible.

Email is a visible option.

Shorter Contact heading, prominent address, copy button and readable fallback. Existing response-time wording retained.

The helper explains itself.

Mail-app behaviour is stated before fields. Timing/budget is labelled optional. “Prepare email” remains accurate.

Actions read cleanly.

Removed the unintended underline from the mobile Contact button. Shortened pricing-gate copy to “Discuss scope and pricing.” The blur remains.

Services has an immediate next step.

Shorter opening copy and a contextual “Discuss a client brief” action, with the agency option selected on Contact.

Small evidence labels are clearer.

Gallery captions now use at least 11px in the adjusted shared components; related-work descriptions/actions are larger. New Chat captions flow together.

The viewer matches the site.

New Chat’s old green image-viewer background is now dark blue. Its close target is 44px. Invisipayment’s concept facts use “Project”.

Craft and usability

Make every element earn its space.

Margins and hierarchy

The shared shell gives the site coherence. The Work opening had stacked generous section paddings; that lead-in is now reduced. Keep generous space around evidence, and use proximity to attach captions and contribution facts to the right content.

Next decision: reduce repeated narrative sections instead of compressing every margin globally.

Images and visual range

The washed-blue staging and natural shells establish a consistent family. Ipiranga and Raiô add variety without losing it. The live Services / ENEM galleries and Raiô laptop check show correct containment and proportions in the inspected views.

Next decision: select images for the job they prove. New Chat’s hero shell is 417px wide at source, and the watch is 344px; larger or high-density display needs better original exports.

Copy and information scent

The Home proposition is specific enough for agency teams. “Selected work” and “Tell me about your project” are clearer destinations. Strong judgement statements identify a choice and its reason; weaker captions merely identify the screen type.

Next decision: replace repeated principles with precise task-level captions. Keep delivery status and concept labels unambiguous.

Contact and control

The header keeps Contact available throughout the long cases. Direct email, copy fallback and honest form wording reduce uncertainty. The image viewer opens with Enter and closes with Escape in the live check.

Next decision: avoid competing paths asking equally for attention. Keep related work compact and subordinate to the final conversation prompt.

Coverage and evidence

A review with clear limits.

Reviewed

Astra read the beta sources. The live pass covered desktop openings for Home, Work, Services, Contact, About, Resume, both service details and all 14 cases. Mobile openings covered the five main destinations and all 14 cases.

Additional gallery inspection: Services Hub, ENEM, Mi Mundo and Raiô. Interaction checks: email copying with clipboard restored, agency preselection, sticky anchor offsets, and New Chat’s keyboard-operated image viewer.

Checks and boundaries

The build/audit passes for all 23 manifest pages: shared styles and chrome, metadata, balanced markup and local references. Inspected desktop/mobile pages showed no horizontal overflow.

This is a heuristic critique in Chrome, not an observed recruiter study, exhaustive interaction audit, assistive-technology audit or physical iPhone/Safari check. No email was sent. Sensitive company figures, portrait replacement and publishing remain outside this pass.

Publication note. Keep beta noindex until you are satisfied. Indexing and machine-readable metadata are already audited for presence; they do not settle commercial claims, content clearance or production SEO readiness.

Principles used

Progressive disclosure supports keeping the brief helper optional and deeper case detail secondary. NN/g: progressive disclosure.

Form effort, clear explanations and appropriate grouping inform the contact improvements. NN/g: web form design, NN/g: reducing cognitive load.

Visible contribution, truthful project status and reliable visual presentation support credibility. NN/g: trustworthy design.

Contrast and usable targets inform the shared controls. The 44px viewer close target is a design choice, not a claim that every target requires 44px. W3C: text contrast, WCAG 2.2.

The recommendations apply these principles to the inspected portfolio. They are hypotheses to validate with agency buyers, not guaranteed conversion improvements.
